Commentary.Commentary: The Windies will now have to score 329 runs if they are to avoid an innings defeat! That score on this wicket, against this New Zealand bowling attack, just seems an uphill task for the visitors. It will be a magical effort and an achievement in itself if they avoid that but that seems highly unlikely. They though will be eager to show some fight and it will be interesting to see if they do fightback. The hosts would want to end this today, 10 wickets is what they need and they have more than 80 overs to go. You have to back them to end it. Can they do so? We will find out.

For New Zealand, it was only the two bowlers who did the job for them, Southee and Jamieson! Both finished with fifers and it is the very first time that two New Zealand bowlers have taken five in the same innings.

End of another poor show with the bat by the Windies. Not a lot you can write about a line-up in which only one guy managed to cross the 20-run mark and it was that man once again who has been the only Windies batter, Jermaine Blackwood. Had it not been for him, it would have been really embarrassing for the visitors. They though have one more chance now to actually show character and some fight with the willow as THE KIWIS HAVE ENFORCED THE FOLLOW-ON!

We are set to begin Day 3. The New Zealand players are out in the middle. Joshua Da Silva and Chemar Holder will resume their innings for the West Indies. Neil Wagner will start the proceedings for Day 3.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the third day of the second Test between the Kiwis and the Windies. This game seems to be heading only one way and that is the hosts’ way. It will probably be a miracle if the Windies manage to avoid a defeat. The question here is, if given a chance, will the Kiwis enforce the follow-on? The visitors need to score another 137 runs to avoid it but that seems unlikely with two wickets in hand. Stay tuned if you want that question to be answered...
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

The hosts will hope they can come out on Day 3 and take the remaining wickets quickly. It will be interesting to see if given a chance, will they enforce the follow-on. Windies, on the other hand, have two debutants out there and they would hope the two can fight back and stay out there for as long as possible. Will that happen? Join us on Day 3 as the action begins at 1100 local (2200 GMT, THE PREVIOUS DAY). Until then, cheers and take care.

The New Zealand bowling was about two people, Southee and Jamieson. The latter is the star with a fifer and the former has the other three which has fallen. The Kiwis were on point with the ball in hand and their work in the field also was top notch as they took a couple of good catches.

The Windies were once again poor with the bat. Once again, it was only Blackwood who showed some resistance and had it not been for him, the Windies would have struggled to get to 100. Blackwood and Brooks did well after Tea, where they were solid and were making sure that they do not lose more wickets but once Brooks fell and then Blackwood followed suit, the rest of their batting just fell apart.
It has all gone brilliantly for the Kiwis. They managed to add close to 175 runs to their overnight score with Nicholls scoring a 150 and Wagner an entertaining half ton.

We really don’t think we need to mention who’s ahead in this game as the score line makes it very evident. Just like the first Test, the hosts are bossing this game too. The Windies are still a lot of runs away from avoiding the follow-on and only a miracle can help them do that.

The West Indies are in a bit of a pickle now and are 4 wickets down. They will be looking at their remaining batters to take them to safer shores and will be hoping that they do not lose any more wickets. The Black Caps, on the other hand, will be looking to continue what they have been doing and will want to restrict the visitors to a small total. An interesting final session of play awaits.

The Kiwis lost their final two wickets after lunch and then started off on the right foot with the ball when they scalped a wicket right inside three overs. It was Southee who started getting rid of Brathwaite. It was Tim again who sent Darren Bravo back to the pavilion, taking a very good catch. Then, it was the magical first over by Jamieson in which he got two wickets on the trot and had two appeals for LBW turned down which has completely turned the tide to the hosts' favour.

Another session where the hosts have been very dominant. They have been brilliant with the bat and have continued that with the ball and the West Indies are clearly on the back foot. Their batters will need to put on a brave show if they are to steady the ship.

On off, pushed to point.
Shamarh Brooks is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! A very, very soft dismissal and Bravo walks back. He will not be happy and he seems in disbelief as he walks back slowly to the shed! Fantastic reflexes from Southee to take this catch so quickly. Full and around off, Bravo looks to push this to the off side but it comes off the inner half of his blade and lob uppishly back towards Southee, who is upto the task and he stretches his hands out and grabs it out of thin air.
Outside off, Bravo leaves it alone.
On off, blocked solidly.
Good length on off, Campbell drives it through covers and picks up a single.
Outside off, John is aware of his off stump and is okay leaving this alone.
FOUR! Beautiful shot! On a good length on off, Campbell drives this through mid off and it runs away to the ropes. Something to cheer about for West Indies.
Down the leg side, Bravo looks to flick but misses.
Outside off, Bravo is comfortable in leaving this alone.

BEATEN! Wonderful bowling by Trent! A full length ball on off, Bravo hangs back in the crease and looks to block this one out but it nips away from the left-hander and misses his outside edge and goes to the keeper.
Outside off, Darren leaves it alone.
A full ball on middle, tucked to square leg.
On a good length on off, Bravo pushes this to the leg side.
On middle, this is pushed back to the bowler.
Now angles this one away from off, it is left alone.
Close! This comes back in from outside off. Campbell leaves it and it goes close past the off pole. Good leave in the end.
Fuller and this one tails back in. It is a little too straight. Campbell looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
The physio comes out to have a look but not sure he can do a lot. John is in some pain. The physio is heading back and Campbell is fine to continue.

OUC!H That has hit Campbell onto the box! This is a length ball and it swings back in late from outside off and also takes off after landing. Campbell looks to play at it at the very end but misses to get hit on the box. He is taking a moment for himself and rightly so.
On off, defended nicely.
Another outswinger, it is outside off. Bravo does not play at it.
Extremely full and gets it to shape away nicely. Bravo jams it out towards covers.
Good swing! On off and it shapes away. Beats the bat of Bravo as he tries to block it.
Angled into the pads, Bravo looks to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.
Angled into the pads, Campbell looks to flick but misses. It hits the pad and rolls down to fine leg. A leg bye taken.
Fuller and on off, it is pushed to mid off.
Fuller and on middle, this is flicked to mid-wicket.
A bumper and on middle, Bravo ducks under it.
Outside off, not played at.
Outside off, this is pushed through covers for two.
An inswinger on middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket.
On middle, defended.
On the pads, tucked towards fine leg for a single.
On off, blocked.
Back of a length on middle, tucked to the leg side.
On off, defended back onto the turf.
Outside off, left alone.
EDGY FOUR! On a good length on off, Bravo looked to defend but it takes the outside edge and goes through the slip cordon into the third man region for a boundary.
On off, pushed through point for a couple.
Outside off, John watchfully blocks this one out.
Length ball on off, pushed to the off side.
Outside off, Campbell does not play at this.
On off, blocked.
FOUR! First boundary of the innings! A good length ball on middle, John tucks this one to the fine leg region for a boundary.
Outside off, left alone.
West Indies finally open their account for this game! On a good length on off, Campbell punches this one through point and they will collect three runs before the fielder can clean up in the deep.
On middle, tucked to the leg side.
Outside off, Campbell looks to drive but gets beaten.
An appeal for caught behind turned down! A back of a length ball, moving away from the batter, John looked to defend but gets beaten and the keeper collects. An appeal but no says the umpire.
Back of a length ball on off, John pushes it out.
On off, blocked.

An appeal for lbw but turned down! A good length ball on middle and leg, shapes back into the right-hander, Bravo looks to push but gets beaten and gets hit on the pads. They appeal but no says the umpire. There might have been an inside edge on this one.
BEATEN! On a good length on off, Bravo looks to drive but gets beaten.
Outside off, left alone.
Who comes in now? It is Darren Bravo.

OUT! CAUGHT! The Kiwis gets their first wicket and it is Brathwaite who walks back to the hut! Brilliant delivery from Southee and Ross Taylor is not going to drop these catches! A back of a length ball around off, nipping away from the right-hander, Brathwaite looks to block this one out but the ball kisses his outside edge and goes towards the first slip, where Taylor takes a very good catch. Kraigg goes for a golden duck. Just the start the Black Caps would have wanted.
On middle, tucked to the leg side.
Fuller around off, Campbell pushes it to covers with soft hands this time. Boult too starts with a maiden.
Back of a length ball on off, John hops and keeps it out to the leg side.
Short of good length on off, Campbell keeps it out off the back foot towards the off side.
Good nut from Campbell! Length ball around off, John comes on the front foot to play at it but the ball goes past the outside edge at the last instance.
Good length ball and shaping away from the batter there as John looks to poke but the ball goes past the outside edge.
Short of good length and around off, played to point.
Fuller and just outside off, Brathwaite lets it go. A maiden to begin with for Southee.
Back of a length ball on off, Kraigg hangs on the back foot and dabs it to gully.
One more ball which is not played at as it is outside off.
Outside off again, this is not played at.
Outside off, left alone.
Down the leg side to begin with! Left alone.
